title: Jerk Chicken
subtitle: Jamaican spiced chicken grilled over charcoal
excerpt: Jamaica's defining dish: chicken pieces marinated in a fiery, aromatic paste of scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme, and spring onion, then cooked over charcoal until charred at the edges and smoky, fragrant, and deeply spiced all the way through.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jerk is Jamaica's most celebrated cooking technique, with roots in the Maroon communities of the island's mountains: escaped enslaved people who preserved their own food traditions over wood fires, smoking and seasoning meat to preserve it and to cook it without producing smoke visible to pursuers. The essential flavourings are allspice (pimento, which grows wild in Jamaica) and scotch bonnet chilli; thyme, spring onion, garlic, and ginger are also characteristic. Traditionally jerk is cooked over allspice wood (pimento wood) in a pit or over a covered barrel grill; the smoke is as important as the marinade. The version here does what it can with a domestic barbecue or a very hot oven: use the grill if you can and charcoal if possible for the closest approximation.

content.text: Marinate for at least 4 hours; overnight gives a much deeper result. Score the chicken pieces deeply through to the bone before marinating so the paste penetrates. Scotch bonnet is very hot; taste the marinade before applying and adjust the number of chillies. Handle scotch bonnets with care: wash your hands immediately after touching.

items.preparation: bone-in, skin-on thighs and drumsticks; scored deeply
1 to 3 depending on heat preference; seeds in for full heat
juice of both; wedges to serve

content.text: Blend all marinade ingredients (scotch bonnet, spring onion, garlic, ginger, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, pepper, salt, soy sauce, oil, lime juice, sugar) to a smooth paste. Score the chicken deeply and rub the paste all over and into the cuts. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.

Grill over charcoal or on a barbecue. Start over indirect heat for 20 minutes, then move over direct heat for 15 to 20 minutes. Turn regularly until the skin is charred in patches and the juices run clear. To oven-cook: roast at 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6 for 45 minutes, then finish under the grill for 5 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve with rice and peas, fried plantain, and lime wedges. The juices from the resting plate are excellent poured over.
